text:
mira: Observed a cluster of failures where the last item in 'actions' array is dropped on int4 canary. Triggers downstream retry loop because toolcall missing.

jon: Any repro sample?

mira: Yes, simplest repro below. Note subtle suffix truncation (missing final array element).
```
Expected:
{"actions":[{"tool":"summarize","args":{"id":1}},{"tool":"notify","args":{"user":"alice"}}]}

Observed:
{"actions":[{"tool":"summarize","args":{"id":1}}]}

Raw tail (hex): 0x7d0a0a -> looks like JSON closed early, sometimes we get a trailing partial token.
```

leah: So we sometimes get an early closing ']' or '}'? That will definitely break strict funcall parsing and cause immediate retry. Is this only int4?

mira: Canary metrics:
- kestrel-mini (int4) actions_trunc_rate: 2.6% over last 4h
- kestrel-lite (int8) actions_trunc_rate: 0.4%
- kestrel-fp16 actions_trunc_rate: 0.05%

ops-bot: alert created: eng-ml.actions_trunc_rate > 1% for 30m -> @eng-ml on-call

jon: Hypotheses: tokenization boundary shifts under aggressive quant cause final token to be omitted (stream cutoff), or KV cache/batching merges cause emitted EOF earlier. Could also be sampling randomness for long arrays.

leah: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) implement response-sentinel validation that rejects responses with an unexpected early EOF when schema expects non-empty array tail; 2) implement a cheap retry-with-offset where runtime re-asks model to continue from last token if raw output is valid JSON prefix; 3) rescue heuristic that appends a best-effort placeholder element (but that seems risky).

mira: For 2) we can check if response ends in an incomplete token (by running a quick parse+cursor check) and then call /v1/chat.continue with prompt: "continue json only". We already have streaming resume infra for cancelled streams.

jon: Let's quantify. I'll run eval-bench across quant profiles and batch configs:
```
eval-bench --model kestrel-mini --quant int4 --suite funcall-ending-suite --samples 8000 --tags batch_size,kvcache,streaming_mode --out /tmp/kestrel_mini_trunc.jsonl
```
I'll run int4,int8,ptq,fp16.

leah: Capture raw_stream_bytes and final_token_id so we can detect whether EOS token was produced. Add telemetry field: resumed_success (for retry-with-offset).

mira: Also add prompt_template_id and route name to the sample so we can correlate with certain templates that produce long action lists.

ops-bot: deploy: kestrel-mini-int4 v1 -> canary 3% scheduled 2026-03-25T02:30Z by @mira

jon: For immediate hotfix, I prefer retry-with-offset behind a feature flag. Conservative policy: only trigger when JSON prefix parses and last token is partial, and only allow one resume attempt per request. Emit header: X-JSON-Resume: attempted(true|false).

leah: Agree. Also log raw+resumed pairs to quarantine bucket (s3://eng-ml/quarantine/actions-trunc) with PII redaction, 500 sample cap/hr.

mira: On the rescue heuristic anchor: if we auto-insert placeholder elements, we must mark the response as repaired and increment repaired_count; otherwise apps will assume a real tool invocation occurred. I vote we avoid insertion until we have strong evals.

eval-bot: scheduled job: funcall-ending-suite run for kestrel-mini int4 at 2026-03-25T03:00Z by @jon

jon: After bench runs, we'll compare metrics: actions_trunc_rate, resumed_success_rate, downstream_tool_retry_rate, and false_repair_rate. If resumed_success reduces end-to-end retries by >40% and false_repair_rate < 2%, roll to 20%.

leah: I'll open PR for resume-with-offset today and add unit tests for partial-token detection + idempotency.

mira: Thanks. Also let's surface a small dashboard panel showing per-template truncation heatmap so prompt authors can optimize templates.

jon: One more: if truncation correlates with specific batch sizes, we might tune runtime default batching for low-latency tool-heavy routes.

leah: Noted. I'll include batch_size sweep in the bench.

mira: Great. We'll reconvene after the bench results.
